reviews.comment: great prof overall, took him last year and his feedback and approach made things super easy. as long as you pay attention in class n do the hw you should be completely fine. tbh, even if you dont, looking over the in-class activities and slides will keep you on top

Dr. Lenfest was awesome. Lectures were clear and informative, and the in-class lecture activities were great immediate application. He was very helpful in office hours and made sure you understood the concept. Provided tons of practice for the midterm and final- would definitely recommend doing all of it. Genuinely cared about student feedback.
ENGR 216 is just not structured well, but Lenfest is a good lecturer. He can be a bit quiet but he is much better than the other profs and assigns less homework than them.

Very chill prof and good lecturer. The final was fine if you studied a week in advance and did his extra practice. Truly cares about his students. Just hope you get lucky with ur lab TA lol (not related to Dr. Lenfest).
A lot of criticism is due to the course structure, not the prof. He did provide a ton of resources to help us succeed, so please use those!

Lectures might put you to sleep sometimes, but he's caring and tries to prepare you for the behemoth that is the 216 final through well-made slides and additional problems. Also, he's really lenient on late work. Would take him relative to other professors.

really chill dude, lectures boring. everyone goes into the final with an A. LOCK IN for the labs so your final exam can be lower, go see the TAs for advice or look to over labs etc. final was similar to practice problems and wasn't completely obscure. actually do the homework and the all the practice problems + optional stuff given. you got this :)

ENGR 216 is a really hard class. He's good at explaining concepts clearly in a way that's easy to understand. He also genuinely cares about your success, if you ever have a question or need clarification on something he's very responsive to emails outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very good at explaining the material clearly in a way that is easy to understand.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Didn't get much of an impression of Dr. Lenfest throughout the semester. Lectures are boring but have practice problems. He provides a TON of resources on canvas. Use them. Allowed us to correct midterm up to 100%. Overall, he cares, but the class is structured poorly, so he's not a bad choice.

His lectures feel a bit boring at times, but if you pay attention all the exams are really easy; there's not much difficult content in the exams. He really cares about the students and will help you if you have any questions.

Dr. Lenfest is a good professor. His lectures can be a bit boring at times but he is the most caring professor I've ever had. He truly wants success for all his students. Just do your work and go into the final exam with an A and you'll be fine.

Dr. Lenfest is a great professor who truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Much of the animosity towards him is more in regards to the course material rather than his teaching quality. The course can be difficult depending on how good of a coder you are, but Dr. Lenfest will do his best to help you out however he can.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests can be difficult but the extra credit is helpful and he grades rather leniently on group assignments. His lectures aren't the best but he's very understanding and easy to talk to if you don't understand the material.

I took Professor Lenfest for ENGR 102 for Fall 2025. He was pretty boring in lecture, and it was easy to get carried away in class. He does give a lot of homework, some of it very tough, but he's very caring and easy to meet outside class. If you have a better choice, take that professor, but he's decent too.

Very relaxed and consistent professor. He typically makes his lectures short and highlights what exactly you need to know for each exam, and allows groups to work on their assignments without much interference. He is always happy to help, and he offers generous extra credit!

Professor reads from the slides (quite comprehensive) but is very understanding and gives plenty of time to work. Quizzes are almost exactly like the practice quizzes given in canvas. Exams are tricky but alright, make sure to know specific cases (stars in slides).

This class is largely based on labs, many of which are group projects (especially the end project), and quizzes, which really test you on the weird edge cases of programming. The lectures (about half of the classes) are fairly boring but pretty much everything in them is important.

He is a great professor overall. His lectures are pretty boring if you are not used to them being so monotone, but they do cover all the material needed for the course. The quizzes aren't really that bad as long as you do the practice quiz. Also, he rounds up your final grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lenfest is a very kind professor and easily accessible out of class. His lectures can be a little monotonous, but that's just how the ENGR102 content is. There are lots of homework assignments, but nothing that is truly 'hard'. The exams are tricky but practice tests and practice problems prepare you well for them.

Great professor he is very chill and super helpful. He also doens't mind if you submit some labs late. Practice quizzes are the same as quizzes. Pray you get a good group because you will spend the whole semester with them.

Lectures are nothing special, he usually just reads off the slides. Responds to emails very quickly. Your experience in ENGR 102 is very dependent on if you get a good group or not. He gets a pity star because his car got hit during my class this semester.

ENGR 102 is a pretty common course so the material is not his fault. As a professor, his lectures are a bit dull, but he is super kind and I really liked him.
The material is annoying but anytime I needed/wanted to miss, he made it no big deal and I could always make up missed material later.

He was meh. Like it wasn't life changing, but his extra credit saved me.

Also I had trouble with a lab one weekend and emailed him, and he gave me and extension, so he is generous about those.

The content is not taught as well as it should have, and he just read off the slides. I also didn't know coding and had to study outside a lot cuz of that.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Lenfest reads the slides that's about it. However if you have questions he will answer very thoroughly and point you in the right directions during labs and other projects. For this course the professor isn't the issue but the material. if you are new to coding this course 'may' be a bit tricky else it's a breeze if you have prior info.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: ENGR 216 is horribly designed with a final exam average of 55-60. No matter who you take your entire grade comes down to one really difficult final. That being said Lenfest made life before the final easy while at least trying to prepare us for it. Lectures are boring but 9/10 times the information you need is in the lecture slides that he post.

I think he was a fine professor nothing outstanding or bad the class mostly is based on the labs which aren't that bad aslong as your teammates arent bums. The hw and quizzes are fairy easy and he allows full points back in the midterm so everyone goes into the final with an A. The final is hard but not impossible I got a 62 on it but kept my A

I'm changing my review from 2 to 5. Up to the first 2 test Lenfest was kind of a dick. As the year went on, he actually became chill. There's a ton of homework but Lenfest also gave us plenty of extra credit. He might not be a great lecturer, and his handwriting might be bad, but he made up for it on exam 3 and the final. Thanks Dr. Lenfest.

Tons of hw but chilled out later. He's not great at teaching but makes up for it by caring abt ur grade. good partial credit + chance for extra credit. the midterms were insanely hard (scores avg 65) but he allows for corrections for half credit. Thought the final was gonna be terrible, we studied a ton but it turned out to be a ez. Thanks Dr.Lenny

Pretty middle of the road, did his job well enough. Boring lectures though. If you need extra help, he's open to giving it, though may come off as slightly annoyed with questions if you ask in person. The class overall is extremely easy to get a high A until the final, but the final is not nearly as hard as people made it seem, with him at least.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of homework in this class. But he genuinely cares and asks for feedback and changes, throughout the semester he tried lightening up the workload. Averages for exams have been below a 70 so he's given corrections for half points back. He makes himself available for students, take advantage of this! I would suggest watching videos before class.

Im on statics round 2. Its hard no matter who you take. The difference is that Lenfest wants you to learn, takes feedback on how he can improve and actually listens. 
Only 3 exams and you can get half points back + tons of extra credit.
Watch Jeff Hanson before class and take Lenfest if you want a decent caring dude and not a patronizing maniac.

The class may be difficult if you don't know python and I don't think the slides will be helpful. If you already know any you should be fine until the end of the semester. There are simple weekly group coding projects with a random team you get assigned at the beginning. He was good about explaining things and what to do if you just asked him.
Decent professor, sometimes a little monotone but genuinely cares, and is willing to help if you ask.

He was pretty alright, he spoke perfect English and was pretty nice once you got to know him. His class was extremely difficult, but he told me if he had the power to change how the class was structured, he would. But since this class is universal for all engineering majors, he can't. Do all the labs and you should be fine.

DO NOT TAKE HIM! His lectures are boring and he just reads off the slides, offers little help or feedback when you ask questions, and DOES NOT CURVE. Take anyone else. He does not prepare you for exams. For the first exam, we covered the last topic on the exam A DAY before the exam, so we had no time to study or properly prepare. Do not take!!

This class is an okay introduction to Python coding. Your grade is mainly dependent on the weekly labs and two exams that you'll take. Professor Lenfest is knowledgable in coding, and can help you work out issues in your code, but the lectures aren't great at learning the content. The exams are the worst part, so try your best to study lots before.

The class isn't terrible, but goes from 0 - 100 very quickly if you have no background in coding. Most of the class is group work so just hope your in a group with good people and start studying early for midterm and final early as they are most of your grade. Lenfest neither adds or detracts from the class, he's fine his TAs do most of the work.

I'm not sure why his rating is low. He is very helpful when asking questions and is extremely responsive through email. He curves the class and gives plenty of opportunities to receive a good grade if you put in the work. I learned a lot in his class and recommend him to anyone who has never coded.

He isn't the worst teacher in ENGR 102 as he doesn't give us as much homework as the others. He gets the concept out but the lectures may be boring sometimes and the class may be a little difficult if you don't have prior coding knowledge as he only teaches concepts and not the problem solving thinking behind them. Overall, he's not bad.

Good guy, obviously is incredibly smart and knows what he's doing. Lectures can be boring but are directly from the slides so you don't really have to pay attention. Homework for this class is brutal if you fall behind, and Lenfest provides 0 leniency for late grades without an excused reason. Overall though I enjoyed the class. Good luck everyone!

He seemed to not care at all during lectures, seemed annoyed when you would ask him questions he dodnt answer, not that hard of a class but he could make it better,his lectire portion of the class was the hardest because he gave half caring lectures. If you take him expect to learn the lecture portion of the class on your own

Not sure what to think about this prof, think he was a victim of a poorly designed class that he wasn't passionate about teaching. Needs better quality examples in class. Basically everyone has a 100 going into the final which is impossibly difficult. You basically need a 65 on the final to get an A in the class. (The average is lower than a 65.)

Honestly not as bad as the reviews put him. His lectures can be boring, but he is helpful if you ask him questions 1 on 1 and makes himself available if you need help. Gives 2 attempts on quizzes and allows you to check HW answers unlike other profs. HW and Labs usually a free 100. Final not bad if you do the practice and he curves final grade.

A decent professor, his lectures are straight from the powerpoint so there really isn't much 'teaching' going on. There is a lot of homework, which takes quite some time to do if you are lost. Quizzes are not too bad, again if you are lost you may have trouble, most questions are straight off of his slides. Responds to emails, within a day or two.

Dr. Lenfest is a boring lecturer, but gives free points through 2 atmpt quizzes and a way to check hw answers. ENGR 216 is genuinely the most unorganized and poorly made class I've ever taken. Labs are honestly weird+confusing and my TAs were not helpful. BE WARNED: the final is nothing like material covered in lecture (resulting in ~40% average).

The lectures are frighteningly boring. Attendance is only important for in-class quizzes. His handwriting is amazingly illegible. Expect a silent class full of students completing individual work during lectures.

I enjoyed the course overall. Weekly individual/group labs are the only work for this class but can be very difficult and time consuming in the 2nd quarter. Midterm and Final are extremely difficult. However, he is very lenient and gives very generous extensions for anything if you have a reason. Our final grades got curved by a whole letter grade.

Overall, he himself is unremarkable. His lectures are very boring and you could probably do very well in the class without ever attending. Most of the time he just reads off of the slides and answers a few questions that could have been answered by a google search. The only reason why I didn't rate him lower is that he is understanding and kind.

He was pretty helpful to me overall. With 102, its more about the TA's than the professor in my opinion. They are the ones that helped me the most for this class, and I've heard similar things about other sections. He was a nice guy and easy to understand so I would recommend him. Take advantage of TA's though for 102, they want to help.
I honestly don't recommend this prof. He was not helpful at all during office hours or in class and his lecture were so boring.

Engr 102 is a difficult class for people with no coding experience and you really want a good professor to learn. Prof. Lenfest reads from premade slides and is very monotone. The tests are very difficult for this class and I feel that he did not provide a lot of help for preparing for them. His practice quizzes were nice but overall, he is okay.

Lenfest was awesome for 102. had no coding experience but his class was fairly easy because he would lecture in depth. Lectures could be boring at times but were helpful when paying attention. was also a lenient grader and was very understanding.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lenfest read off slides every Monday in class for an hour and that was our learning for the week. It is not enough lecturing to provide you with enough info to complete the labs which get very difficult towards the end of the semester. It is crucial to do good on the quizzes. 2 exams, both very difficult. I had to get 2 tutors to pass this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I believe the difficulty of this course mainly comes from the content, not the professor. Still don't prefer him

He is very understanding and does well with feedback. He is very monotone though and only reads off the lecture slides. Doesn't provide outside knowledge. Good guy, chose the wrong profession. It's impossible to listen to him when he's lecturing but he is always ready to help if you have a question.

Get a good group that knows how to code or you're screwed the whole semester. He gave quizzes ONCE a week which was ok. The exams were very difficult. He is a nice guy but the lectures were BORING. Every Friday I was in office hours, no joke, for help. This is supposed to be an "into" to coding, it isn't. If you don't know how to code, good luck.

216 is structured poorly with too much content to cover in a 50-minute weekly lecture, but Lenfest is a decent prof. He is easy to access and helpful with homework. It is very difficult to prepare for the final exam because it tests on obscure things not covered in class but he makes it easy to get a high grade before the final to act as a buffer.

I had him for CLEN 181 but I can't find that on here. He just read off of the slides and seemed like he really didn't wanna be there. I also heard he's not that good for 102 from a friend. Try taking a different prof.

I found this class to be pretty difficult after the midpoint of the semester. I just skipped the lectures because he'd read verbatim from the slides and wasn't very useful. The two exams that you take were pretty difficult as someone who's already coded in Python. However none of the activities in ZyBooks were mandatory like other professors

Dr. Lenfest is a good person, but I didn't enjoy him as a professor. His lectures are long, boring, and he tends to read off the slides instead of trying to teach. His exams are difficult as is the class if you don't have previous experience with coding. He is available for office hours which were helpful, but I recommend a different professor.

Dr. Lenfest was a great guy and knows his stuff. My only complaint is that the lectures could get a bit monotone at times so I would just review the slides myself later. Final was tough so make sure you study for it well.
Dr. Lenfest is a good guy who cares about his students. Easy to do well in his class if you pay attention and turn stuff in.

He is very understanding and respectful. The TA's do the grading and sometimes they mess up. The course is heavy on coding but the lectures aren't his so he can't do much other than read it which can be frustrating sometimes. He has a monotone voice so distraction kind of just happens. A lot of the work is coding with the group so make sure to help

Despite the negative reviews, Dr. Lenfest is a great teacher. More so in a personal learning experience. Most of your questions can be answered from the lecture slides, but if not he is awesome 1 on 1. He is extremely understanding and is always willing to work with you. If you can get Dr. Lenfest, I highly suggest you take him.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy but doesn't treat it as an intro to coding. He doesn't really teach, he just reads off the slides that do NOT teach you how to code. Spend more than extra time watching Python youtube videos. Lab instructions often unclear as well.

I have never coded before and this course seemed like a good introductory into most of the basic concepts of programming. Dr.Lenfest would answer all my questions and provide a ton of help. I was lucky and got a good group for my projects so that made that portion of the class significantly more enjoyable. Overall, very doable class.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't particularly exciting but he was very helpful anytime you had issues. Accessible outside of class and overall taught me to actually code which two previous teachers had failed at. You have to put in considerable effort as there is a lot of homework but overall a very good professor.

Yes he is bland in his lectures, but he is very understanding and is always willing to help out as long as you communicate. He truly cares about his students understanding so always ask questions after lecture!

He seems like a super nice guy, but he just reads off the slides in a boring and monotone voice. If you already know Python, this class is already a breeze and you might as well take him. If you are new to Python or programming in general, I strongly recommend you look for other professors. Python is an easy language when taught well.

He really doesn't teach, but to be fair you can't really teach coding you can kinda have to learn through trial and error. His lectures are boring, but he does posts the slides. He is also pretty lenient on when quizzes are due. For the most part he really didn't teach how to code, but gave us the tools to learn ourselves.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lenfest isnt too bad. He can be kinda boring in his lectures, but its pretty tolerable. Really just reads off of slides. He does record his lectures and posts slides, so its very helpful after lectures. Homework isnt too heavy, but he does do quizzes in class. Class wasnt easy, but it also wasnt hard.

Lenfest is a meh professor, but a gentle type-of guy. Be warned because ENGR 102 is a very difficult class, especially if you do not have prior coding experience. The problem is, he does not really make his lessons and class engaging. He is very soft spoken. The good news is, he can be reached outside of class for help. Not the best, not the worst.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures were always very dull and it seemed like he didnt want to be there. He would just read off the slide in a low voice and keep going. If you're new to coding like I was, I do not recommend him because it will be tough. The HW was very time consuming and frustrating. The Zybooks textbook was extra credit towards your final grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bland lecturer, but it was his first time teaching the course. Homeworks are frustrating because there's few examples to go off other than 2  the lecture slides. Do the homework before his class or office hours, then ask him about the problems you don't get. He is very willing to help. Final exam avg was a 45 which is normal for this dumb course.

Good guy, bad lecturer. I'm pretty studious, but often fell completely asleep in lectures. Lots of homework and assignments and lab reports that are graded really tough, but are doable. Class curriculum is all over the place, so the comprehensive final at the end can be an absolute nightmare if you don't study in a mature, prepared manner.

I passed this class by 0.73 points... pure luck. If you can avoid him, please don't take Lenfest. And if you do, find a friend with a different prof to teach you. He can't teach. He reads off the slides but doesn't explain any further.

Dr. Lenfest isn't horrible, but he definitely isn't good. He's obviously new at teaching and his lectures/homework did not prepare me for the final at all. He also makes his homework much more time-consuming than other profs, but it does help some in the end. The labs are the most important part of this class so work hard on them!

Don't take Lenfest if you have the choice. His "lectures" were him breezing through powerpoints so fast that I couldn't even take notes on them. He has negative personality when lecturing, and one time when my group asked him for help he looked a it, said  "that's wrong," and walked away.

While I did perform ok in this course, I would not recommend Dr. Lenfest to anyone when looking for a ENGR 102 course. While there is a "lecture", it's really just a brief run through of a PowerPoint and maybe a super easy example before your on your own to figure out much more difficult questions.

Professor Lenfest was not very helpful over the length of this course. His lectures are sleepy and composed of powerpoints which are skimmed through without much elaboration. As an intro course to engineering/code I felt that it was very unfavorable to students especially those that aren't entering a computer/tech related major after freshman year.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Unless you already know how to code do not take him for engineering 102. He doesn't really teach the material and instead skims through 50 slide PowerPoints without really explaining anything about the PowerPoints. Also some of the quizzes are unnecessarily hard without a curve regardless of how bad everyone does.

Absolute worst experience freshman year. I wish this class could be more fun, but it is dreadful because of professor lenfest. Very unapproachable inside and outside of class. The quizzes are weighted too heavily. Not friendly at all, very cold, and even aggressive at times.

Professor Lenfest did not take into Account that this is supposed to be a basic course designed for people with no coding experience. His grading scale was challenging because the quizzes were too heavily weighted. Zybooks is optional but should have been mandatory. Gave huge project over thanks giving break. Would never use this prof again

For Engr-102 in the fall he taught his class mostly through lectures that would then lead into 2 weekly code assignments that would be graded on Mimir, a system that has to have the perfect output. Additionally his two exams were very hard to prepare for if you did not buy the nonmandatory study textbook. He did not prepare us for the exams at all.

Told us Zybooks is optional, skipped several topics vital for doing labs and did not explain where we could find what we needed. His grading standard at the moment is terrible where 4 question quizzes can completely invalidate 5-6 hours of work on individual labs. Quizzes will absolutely crush your grade if you have no coding experience
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Lenfest, as a person, is fantastic. Very nice and caring individual. However, it isnt a super good professor. He is absolutely brilliant but his explanations for questions tend to be rather confusing. The coding assignments can be difficult especially as a student with no prior experience. He is decent but be prepared to struggle.

If you come in with coding experience (it's a python class), it should be a breeze. However, if you haven't coded before, you'll have to do some self-studying, as Lenfest is very boring and quiet, and the best way to learn the material is through hands-on experience. As long as you put in the effort and find resources, it should be an easy class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria
